utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honours, Laurie Sartorio and Kyle Wood for the Prosecution. We're assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to my colleagues, the Prosecution. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson for the Defence of General Rasim Delic, and appearing with us is the legal assistant, Lana Deljkic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I've been told we should hold court with the witness for some time because, Ms. Sartorio, you have something to say?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour. As you know, this witness is coming. She is a forensic pathologist who examined the bodies that were exhumed that were the subject of a previous witness's testimony. More than 30 days ago, we filed a motion -- a notice to present this expert witness, and attached to that motion was what we thought was the full report of the expert as well as her statement. They were attachment A and B to our notice of expert testimony. We discovered recently, in fact last Friday, that one -- half of her report was not attached, and the reason is half of her report was in a different ERN range. Somehow it got split up, but it was discovered, and I tried to give Defence counsel a copy over the weekend, but somehow there was a miscommunication between security. I left it with them and they never got it. However, having said that, the second half of the report -- the first half of the report discusses bodies 1 through 7. The second half of the report discusses body number 8 and skulls A through H. Defence counsel has had this second half of the report disclosed to them quite some time ago. The bodies 8 and skulls A through H were discussed in the statement of Dr. Silajdzic-Brkic, and there is mention of it in all of the disclosure as well as the exhibit that is on the list for this doctor. What was simply missing was the final -- the final report -- her report that was written on body number 8 and skulls A through H. Some of the -- all but -- only two of the skulls are actually relevant to our crime base, so in fact it's not -- none of this is a surprise to the Defence, and at this point the Prosecution seeks to supplement the exhibit list with the second half of the doctor's report, as well as being able to submit it in evidence today through the doctor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Sartorio. Madam Vidovic, anything to say, or Mr. Robson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. The position is that the Prosecution filed its motion to -- and submitted the expert report on the 25th of September. The motion was submitted pursuant to Rule 94 ter, which concerns experts. Moreover, on the 1st of October, the Prosecution filed an addendum to that motion, and as part of that addendum, the Prosecution provided an English translation of the expert report. Now, the expert report only deals with bodies number 1 through to number 7. Body number 8 isn't there, and as are -- and the skulls are also not mentioned. However, it's the Defence's submission that that was the expert report that the Prosecution chose to file, and under Rule 94 ter the Prosecution were obliged to file the full report and/or statement. That's what the Rule says. And the Defence had a period of time, 30 days, in order to respond. When the Defence responded, we responded on the basis of the document that was filed with the Court. Now, this witness was due to testify on Friday, and the Court is aware of the reasons why the witness did not proceed to testify that day. And on Friday, as far as the Defence were concerned and as, it seems, as far as the Prosecution was also aware, that witness would have testified on the basis of the expert report that was filed back in September. Now, having adjourned the case early on Friday, it seems that the Prosecution has now discovered that there is a second part to this report. The Prosecution contacted the Defence over the weekend to say that there was this further part which had not been filed. The Defence was informed that a copy of that document would be left with -- in the locker and then told it would be with the Security over the weekend. We attempted to obtain that document. It wasn't in the locker, and no security officer had a copy of it that they could give to us. Now, today we were able to obtain a copy of the further part of the report in the B/C/S language during the course of the morning. However, at 20 past 2.00, I've just received a copy of that second part in English, and the situation is I simply don't know what that report says, the second part. So there we have it, Your Honour. So it seems that we have a failure to comply with the procedural requirements of Rule 94 ter, and I'm aware of what the doctor may say about body number 8 and the skulls, from what she says in her statement, but I certainly don't know what she says in her expert report. It's a rather unsatisfactory situation. Your Honours, I don't know how far we can really proceed with this, but I'm not really happy for the witness to testify upon the contents of the second report, the further report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You know, when this motion was filed on the 25th of September, and I'm aware that the Chamber became aware of the fact that it was already short notice, and I don't know whether we did discuss it in court or not -- we did. Mr. Tillman confirms, because I remember we discussed it. The Defence is entitled to 30 days to respond, and if you give notice on the 25th of September for a witness to testify on the 25th of October, you're already out of time. We raised this then, because the Defence was entitled, up until the 25th of October, to respond to that motion like they have responded.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. They did respond earlier, which is why we put the witness back on the list. In other words, they didn't use the full 30 days to respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right. And so they were still accommodating you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. And let me just, if I may, emphasise, though, that, first of all, the document was disclosed, so the information was there. The information was discussed in the statement of Dr. Brkic, which is also attached to our notice. And the translation was disclosed on the 21st of August of 2007 of that additional -- that second half of the report. And furthermore, with the last witness, both the Prosecution and the Defence discussed the ICMP DNA reports where -- exhibit 649 and 645 where they include in the DNA reports the DNA analysis of body 1/8 and of a couple of the skulls, so the DNA reports of those two items have been submitted in evidence. So the report, for the purpose of completeness -- and also under 94 bis it says "the full statement and/or report of any expert witness shall be disclosed," and we did disclose the full statement, and the second half of the report was omitted not intentionally. But the witness can testify also about what she did, the procedure she followed, without the report, but we're just -- we're trying to ensure that the record is complete, and the witness is here, and there doesn't appear to be, in our opinion, any prejudice to the accused, since they had the information and the information is already included in exhibits that have been admitted in evidence and was included in her statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At least speaking for myself, I know I've got the first part of the report, too, I haven't got the second part as we speak, it was one of the questions I was going to raise with the witness as to where is the eighth body and where are the skulls, but I don't know how long this second portion is. Is it something, Mr. Robson, that the witness couldn't sort of just read in B/C/S in court and you could -- it could be translated?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: We have the English translation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How long is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It's eight pages, Your Honour -- 30 -- pages 7331 to 7338 of the ERN range.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, it's the whole report, the entire report now, 16 pages of which seven deals with the further part which hasn't previously been disclosed as part of the expert report. And if I might just say so, Your Honour, just to respond to something else that my learned friend mentioned a moment ago, it is right to say, now that we've been able to check the records, that the English translation was disclosed earlier this year, but it wasn't mentioned as being part -- as being a "PT," i.e., an exhibit which the Prosecution was intending to use within this case, and the information that came with this disclosure relating to this additional part of the expert report states: "Documentation relating to exhumation of the Kamenica area, Zavidovici Municipality, on 26th June 2006, received from the Cantonal Prosecutor's Office in Zenica exhumed corpses ..." and then there are some names. So there's nothing in the information that was supplied to suggest that this was part of Dr. Sabiha Brkic-Silajdzic's expert report. So in the absence of something to say it's a "PT," in the absence of something to say this is connected to the expert's report, we didn't really -- it simply wasn't brought to our attention, in our submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Madam -- you see, I work more with you than I work with Madam Sartorio. Every time I want to say "Madam Sartorio," I say "Madam Vidovic." Madam Sartorio, I'm afraid you have to lead the evidence on the first seven bodies. If you want to lead her on the eighth body and the heads, you can to do so at a later stage. You'll have to reschedule her. We feel that in fairness to the Defence, you just can't lead her on the second part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, it's rather awkward to start leading her on part of her testimony and then have her cross-examined, and then we're going to ask to bring her back for the second part of the testimony; is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want them to postpone?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, rather than -- I think that might be the best thing, under the circumstances. We'll give them the 30 days' notice, postpone her to the end of the month, if that's what's required. We can't afford not to have this in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fine, it's up to you. If you want to postpone, then we can postpone, and you file that report properly and give them proper notice. That's fine, if that's what you want to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio, how long would your examination-in-chief be?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I was going to stay within my time allotted today, which I believe was an hour and a half. I was going to try to shorten it. I think what the doctor will testify to is quite straightforward, and it's a matter of getting in the records through her and her talking about her examination. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Because rather than completely losing her today, we could at least start and then you could finish your examination-in-chief, and then we could postpone and call her back.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: How about we suspend my examination-in-chief, because if we say we have no further questions, we're ending it at that point. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, you'll be able to continue when we then get the second part and call her back.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That would be fine, Your Honour. I'm prepared to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Rather than just losing the time now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd be prepared to do that, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then before you call her, there's just a small other housekeeping matter. The Chamber has sort of been notified of the availability of sessions in the morning this week, that we could sit, if we would like, in the morning rather than in the afternoon, and we thought that tomorrow and Thursday we could indeed take advantage of sitting in the morning, if everybody is agreeable. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I believe that's fine, Your Honour, with the Prosecution. The next witness is not going to be ready to start until tomorrow, however. He's still in proofing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, that's fine. So we can call this one, and as soon as we finish with this housekeeping matter. Last week, when we talked about accommodating this witness, we did not finally say whether we are sitting or not sitting on Friday. So we are not sitting on Friday, okay, in line with the order that we gave of sitting four days. Okay, thank you so much. You may call the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The Prosecution calls the doctor. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It looks like we have lost the witness, so let's take a short adjournment. We'll be called once she's been found. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ma'am. Would you please stand up. Good afternoon, ma'am. Madam, please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may please be seated now. Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Madam, would you please -- would you please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: My name is Sabiha Silajdzic-Brkic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And in what municipality and country do you currently reside?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: I reside in Visoko, Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: At present, I am a forensic medicine expert, and I do forensic work, autopsies. I have worked on exhumations, and a few days ago I completed my specialisation in cytology, so my duties have been expanded in the hospital and I'm now in the oncology ward.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And could you please tell the Judges about your education, and particularly in the field of forensic pathology?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: I graduated from the Faculty of Medicine in Sarajevo, specialising in forensic medicine in Ljubljana, that is, I went to Ljubljana to specialise, and after that I continued working and I completed seminars and courses that were organised in our country mostly by foreign experts. There was a DNA laboratory extraction course. I don't deal with that anymore. Then I undertook anthropological courses that we needed when working in exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us when you graduated from the Faculty of Medicine in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And since 1990, have you been involved in exhumations and/or the examination of bodies recovered during exhumations?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: I did exhumation first between 1990 and 1995, when I worked at the War Hospital in Tesanj, and I worked in triage, the triage of wounded persons, and that was the first time that I encountered injuries of that type. In 1995, I started my specialisation course, which I completed in 1999, which means that for eight years I had been working independently, and for four years I dealt with exhumations, that is to say, from 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us approximately how many exhumations you have dealt with?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact figure because I never liked adding up the numbers, because every exhumation is independent and separate, so -- but, anyway, during my work, I have worked with over 1.000 bodies. I worked on individual cases, bodies on the surface. I dealt with mass graves and secondary graves, actually, primary graves and secondary graves as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And has your work been primarily focused in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Have your exhumations been -- have they taken place in the former Yugoslavia or other countries, for instance?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: No, only on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in the canton I live in, the Central Bosnian Canton of Travnik and from time to time for the Sarajevo Canton as well, but my first exhumations were conducted during my specialisation course in 1995, when I was member of the first team that was ever established, the expert team of forensic experts in Tuzla, and that's when I first had to deal with bodies that were from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just get clarification, ma'am. Do you deal with exhumations or do you deal with autopsies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The procedure in our country is as follows: A physician dealing with autopsies is usually present on exhumation sites, which means that my work begins with exhumation. I am present during the exhumation process, when the bodies are dug up. I follow the body and then complete the process with an autopsy. In exceptional cases, if you cannot assist an exhumation, which has been prevalent of late, or if anthropologists from the ICMP are present who can follow the body, then it's not compulsory for a physician to be on the spot, on the terrain, at all times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you present when the bodies you're about to testify about were exhumed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So in this case, you're going to testify about autopsies, not exhumation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just wanted to get that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us, over the course of the last 12 years approximately how many autopsies that you have been involved in?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Well, as I said with the bodies, certainly over 1.000. I can't give you an exact figure.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you now to talk to -- to explain to the Chamber what is involved when you are asked to participate in an autopsy, and particularly one where you did not attend the exhumation site. What is the first course of action that takes place?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: This is a rare case where I did not attend the exhumation process itself. Usually, I did. But when I am not present at the exhumation, then my assistant is on site, and he's been working for me -- with me for many years, and I have trained him how a body should be followed and how bodies must be exhumed, because when you discover a body in a grave, my assistant comes up to the body, cleans it, and he takes out the body, not the workers digging up the actual area. So in this case, I continued working on the bodies once they arrived in Visoko. When the bodies were in Visoko, we received information -- or rather I received information that I should not touch the bodies until representatives of both committees for missing persons were present, our federal commission and the commission of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Let me just stop you there. When the Judge just asked you, "Are you present when the bodies you're about to testify about were exhumed," you answered no and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm confused now and I just want to make sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So are you or are you not generally present during the actual exhumation?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Generally, yes. Maybe just because of the last two or three -- or rather for the last two or three exhumations, when I was doing additional training, I was not, but otherwise I followed the whole procedure from Day 1 to the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I would like to direct your attention to June of 2006, and -- well, before I do that, sorry, excuse me, one more question. Have you ever testified in court in relation to your work?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have, in our courts, the Cantonal Court in Travnik, and also in one case I gave a statement at the State Prosecutor's Office in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And on what topics would you -- have you testified on in relation to your work; your particular examinations and autopsies of bodies? And if so, can you be particular about what it is you testified?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Well, specifically, they were injuries that were found on the bodily remains of the persons and to determine what body it was, whether the bodies were identified. In these cases, the two bodies were identified, and on the basis of my examination of the body, I made my findings, whether there were fractures or injuries during transport, perhaps, or because the body had been buried underground for a long time or maybe above ground, depending on where the body was lying.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And have you also testified, in relation to your work, about cause or manner of death of when -- of the remains, the mortal remains?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: In my country, it's difficult to explain to people that when I have a skeleton, I cannot determine with 100 per cent certainty the cause of death. The word "autopsy," in my country, means "postmortem," and that means an entire examination of the body, with the abdominal cavity, the contents in the skull, and the general body, so I call this an osteological examination, because if I only look at the bones, that is not a complete autopsy, it is just an autopsy of the remains that have been found and not the entire body. And so for that reason, if I might be allowed to continue, you cannot give the cause of death, because I always like to give the example of a man with a fractured rib, you don't die of a fractured rib, but I no longer have the lungs to examine so I cannot say what affect that fractured rib had on the lungs and determine the actual cause of death.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And for my purposes, as well as probably the Judges', maybe they know, but "osteological examination," can you tell us what that means?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Osteology is the science of bones. Therefore, an osteological finding means a finding based on an examination of the bones.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But I believe you just said that an autopsy in your country means the entire examination of the body, including the abdominal cavity, contents of the skull, et cetera, and then you said that you called that an osteological examination, so that to me means more than bones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Calls that autopsy, but when she's given the bones only --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Osteological.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- the skeleton only, then she --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- does an osteological examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now I would like to direct your attention to June of 2006, and I would like to ask you if you participated, first of all, in an exhumation? If so, where, and if not, did you participate in an examination of bodies that had been exhumed?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: In 2006, as far as I can remember, I know that I wasn't there in June because I was doing additional training and I did not attend any exhumations at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But did you examine some bodies that had been exhumed in June of 2006?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I examined the bodies. More specifically, the bodies that we are talking about today. After that, I had certain individual bodies that were subsequently found in other locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, do you recall the -- do you recall the date of an exhumation that is going to be the subject of your discussion today?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Usually, as part of my written findings, I indicated the date of the order based on which I started the autopsy. The order was issued on the 27th of June, 2006.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us -- and I'm going to show you a document in a minute, but can you tell us if you know -- I think you just said you weren't in the region. Was that the reason why you did not attend the exhumation? You were doing additional training, is that why you didn't attend the exhumation?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: That's the reason, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May the witness be shown document P02964, page 22 in English and 14 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, Doctor -- the first page of -- I would like to ask, looking at the document in front of you, if you can identify what this document is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just would like to point out that the documents don't correspond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Apparently the documents do not correspond, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: You're right. Just a second, Your Honour. If we could go to page 22 in English. Is that 22? Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio, you're saying, "Go to page 22," but is this the correct document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I believe the B/C/S document is the correct one, not the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then you can't go to page 22 in the English because then the English is not the correct one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right. Well, my page for this document was 22, so I need the English translation of the document that is on the screen. My case manager is -- it's an order of 27 June 2000 -- page 7? Twenty-seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Twenty-seven.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Twenty-seven, please, thank you. Now that corresponds.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: This is the document that I mentioned as the order of the Cantonal Prosecutor's Office, dated the 27th of June, which assigns me as an expert in the forensic examination of the bodies that were exhumed as per this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And in the first sentence, underneath the word "Order," can you just tell us what that -- what that says?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: That a forensic medical examination be carried out on eight bodies recovered in the Kamenica area, 15 kilometres from Zavidovici, on the banks of the River Gostovic on the 21st, 22nd and 23rd June. Do you want me to read the whole document or do you want me just to summarise and tell you what I am being asked to do?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, no, the answer is, no, I don't want you to read that, and thank you. But I just wanted to identify for the record where this exhumation had taken place, and then you can tell us what this order ordered you to do.

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: When I received a document of this kind, i.e., an order from the prosecutor's office, that document contained the data of the bodies, i.e., when they were exhumed and where. I also received the prosecutor's number, which is very important for me, because that is the number that accompanies the body throughout the procedure. The number is also attached to the samples. This is the number KTA-248/06. The order also states, as you can see here, that I am asked to carry out a forensic medical examination, that I will be asked to carry out anthropologic and osteological and forensic procedure. The anthropological part is the one I've already talked about. In the course of my subsequent trainings, I learned about that. Those are actually osteological examinations. You look at the bones to see whether they are typical in any way, whether they have any special features. For example, on the skeleton you may see whether he had a protruding upper or lower jaw, he or she, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may ask just one little question, ma'am. You just told us, ma'am, you did not attend the exhumation. This order says you did. Are you able to explain the difference? The order says that the examination be carried out by a forensic court expert, Dr. Sabiha Brkic-Silajdzic from Visoko, who was present at the exhumation, and you told us you were not there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see that in this document. It says here that a forensic medical examination be carried out on eight exhumed bodies or recovered bodies, which means that the bodies are already there, not for me to go to the exhumation. When I am supposed to attend the exhumation, the order says that I'm supposed to attend the exhumation and follow that exhumation by the examination. That's how the order reads if I'm asked to attend an exhumation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that, ma'am. There may be a problem with the translation. The English translation, which I am reading, alleges that you attended the exhumation. I just want you to clarify that in relation to what you told us, that you did not attend the exhumation in this particular case. Is it a mistake in the translation? Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may assist, maybe you should ask the witness to read the second passage and you will see that there is no mistake in translation. The examination will be carried out by a forensic court expert who was present, this is a mistake on the part of our prosecutor's office [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's all I wanted to clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we ask this document to be admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Exhibit 653.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sixty-five --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Five three.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And just for the record, this is still part of PT2964. As you know, I'm just admitting certain pages at a time and it will be given different exhibit numbers at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, is it a "PT" or "PO"?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: "PO," 2964, sorry, but it's -- each group of pages out of that range of that pre-trial exhibit number will be a separate exhibit, if that's acceptable to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, you go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, after receiving that order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. Before it disappears from our page, the answer the witness gave, where she confirms that the mistake was on the part of the prosecutor's office, that has not actually been specified in the transcript, so perhaps if that could be -- it appears as though Madam Vidovic has given that answer. I'm sure it will be sorted out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, yes, it seems as if it's Madam Vidovic's answer. Madam Vidovic said, "Your Honour, if I may assist, maybe you should ask the witness to read the second passage and you will see that there is no mistake in translation." And then the witness read. Sorry, Mr. Court Reporter, there's a mixture here. The sentence starting at line 21, page 20, which says: "The examination will be carried out by a forensic court expert who was present, this is a mistake on the part of our prosecutor's office," those words are the witness's words, not Madam Vidovic's words. If you can attend to that, please. You may proceed, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, in terms of your involvement in this -- in the examination of the bodies from this exhumation, was this the first document that you received or was this the first formal document that you received with regard to this task -- tasking?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you review any documents in preparation for the autopsy? In other words, did you review any official reports that were written after the exhumation?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio, if you can clarify for the sake of the Court Usher. This Exhibit 653, you said, is just this order, not the entire pages of the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, the document, I believe, is two pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just the two pages?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to ask the witness to be shown, of the same P02964, page 7 of the B/C/S, page 13 of English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, Doctor, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Have you seen anything that reported a record of the on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Based on my experience, i.e., on our work, I did not need this because I always attended exhumation. In principle, whenever I work, a record of the on-site investigation doesn't hold much importance for me. What is important is the body itself. When I receive a body, I have to examine it, regardless of the circumstances and regardless of the on-site investigation record, which might even divert my attention from the important things. I always insist that on completing the examination of the body, first, without knowing anything else, and in most cases I did not even peruse those records of the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But in this case, you did not attend the exhumation, ma'am. Didn't you then need this record, now that you did not attend this particular exhumation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not need this record, because the bodies were already in the bags, they were all already in the morgue, and everything else would have been superfluous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. So what is the first thing that you did with relation to examining the bodies? Tell us where you went and what you were presented with and by whom.

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: As far as these bodies are concerned, they were rather specific with regard to the other bodies that I had worked on. I received an order to carry out an examination of these bodies. However, I had to wait first for both sides to be present, i.e., the representatives of both commissions, the federal commission and the Republika Srpska commission. A doctor came from Banja Luka, Zeljko Karan, and when we were all together, we took one bag after another, and the first thing we did was to take a DNA sample in the presence of everybody. I believe that there is a record of that somewhere. Usually this was done by the prosecutor's office or the police who were present during this preliminary examination. This was done in order to find a bone that would be adequate for the DNA analysis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't mean to interfere with your leading --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- but we have the expert witness's report. It looks like you're taking her through her report again. Don't you want her to confirm her report and whether she stands by it, and that's it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. I was just laying the foundation for what -- the procedures and how she came to write her report, that's all, but I can move along quite more quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And I'm there at this point. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So are you in Visoko at this point, are you at a morgue, or where are you in looking at these documents, and who's present, other than Dr. Karan that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: I've already told you that I and Dr. Karan together opened the bags, and we were taking samples for the DNA. This is what we had been requested to do by the Prosecutor's Office and by both commissions, and there was also a demand for both sides to be present during that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right, and that's my question. When you say "both commissions," was Mr. Goran Krcmar present?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Let me just explain one thing. When I do my job, I am probably too focused on my part of the job, and as for the things that surround me, I know that there are people who are in charge of that. I mostly focus on my work and on the body. As far as I can remember, and I can't be certain of that, he may have been present.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Now, you examined each -- each bag. Can you tell us, did you write a report after conducting your examination?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: I would just like to add one thing. I said that I was not sure about Goran because he was not that important for my part of the work, but I am sure about Dr. Zeljko Karan and crime technicians who took photographs. So whatever was important for my part of the job, I paid attention to that. This was not a classical examination. We only opened one body after the other. We took photos and we also took samples for the DNA analysis. That's what we did at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you -- may the witness please be shown the same P02964, page 26 in Bosnian and 55 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do we do with page 13? You showed her page 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That -- withdraw it. I mean, we're not seek to admit it. She did not see the document, Your Honour. We'll get it through another witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to please go to the -- to the end of this particular document, which is page 51 in English, I believe -- no, not 51. It's page 15 of the report, which if you look at the bottom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it page 15, ma'am, or page 55?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, in e-court it starts at page 55, and the document starts -- at the bottom you'll see it's document page 1, and the document ends at page 15, which would be 70, page 70 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. And what is the date? I see it says "31st July" and then "20". I beg your pardon, the page is gone now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, could you scroll up to the top of the page, please. Okay. Could you go to the previous page so the doctor can see what number this is. And one more page in English. Okay. And could you please scroll to that page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you identify the cover page of this document, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: What I'm looking at, on the left side of the screen, was the title page or the cover page of my findings, containing the data on the Cantonal Prosecutor's Office, the number of the case, and which prosecutor ordered that the examination be done. Now I'm looking at the first part of my findings, and the bottom of each page contains the same data, making a reference to the prosecutor's office, the name of the prosecutor, and the number of the case. Every page, therefore, bears the same data on the case and on the prosecutor's office who ordered the examination to be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now I'd like you to tell us what this -- does this represent the whole of your report or is this part of the report?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: This is just one part, the end of one body and the beginning of the other body.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us, have you reviewed your report in preparation for your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you stand by your findings and conclusions that are contained in this report?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber how many bodies or body remains that you examined and determined were of -- how many bodies you determined there were?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: When the forensic examination was done, we ended up with eight bodies, of which seven were without a skull. Body number 7 did have a skull, and as for body number 8, we only found fragments of the skull bones. And now what did I describe in this part of the findings? Separate from the body, there were seven skulls, each of them packed into a separate bag.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, do you have information about where the skulls were found in relation to the other remains?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: I asked my assistant, just my assistant and nobody else, where the skulls were found and where the rest of the bodies were found. I am only -- always interested in that in order to understand how the skulls got separated from the body. He told me that the bodies were in one part of the grave, and independent of that, in another part of the grave, there were just the skulls.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us, in terms of your whole report, how you numbered the so-called bodies or body remains? What was the numbering system?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: The numbering system had been in use for a number of years and it had been accepted by the people involved in the DNA analysis and the commissions, because it provides for the easiest monitoring of the body. The markings "1/1", "1/2" and "1/3" indicates that it is one and the same location, i.e., that the eight bodies were found in one location. That is indicated by the number "1" in front of the numbers that mark the bodies. In order to avoid any confusion, the skulls were marked with letters.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us the total number of bodies? In other words, what was the highest number it went up to, "1/1" to "1/" what?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: "1/8" was the final number for the body.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And in terms of the skulls, can you recall the letters, the sequence of letters, how many? The skulls were marked with letters, were they not?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: A, B, C, D, E, F, H, so from A to H.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in terms of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, ma'am. The witness said, "A, B, C, D, E, F, H." She jumped "G," and then she says, "From A to H." From A to H is eight. A, B, C, D, E, F, H is seven, so there's some confusion here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you just hear what the Judge said, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I appreciate your question. I, myself, asked, "What about G," which was supposed to be there, but I suppose that on the ground they got -- they mixed up the alphabet, and I for myself had to follow and keep the markings that were given to the bodies on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So were there seven or eight skulls found?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Seven skulls, because you won't find the "G" skull in my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now I'd like the witness to be shown Exhibit 649 while we are -- and I'll ask a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do you want to do with page 55 --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, Your Honour. We would ask they be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page 55 is admitted in evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number, page 55 of PO2964.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want page 55 or page 55 to 70?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Fifty-five to 70, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 654.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, 649, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, while that's coming up on the screen, Exhibit 649, I'll just ask you: Was -- part of your examination included, I believe you said earlier and it's also in your report, that you took DNA samples from the bones. Could you briefly explain that process to the Chamber? Was every bone tested or how -- what did you do?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: In this case, the reverse was actually done. Every time -- the rule is that the body is examined first to see what we have in the bag, in the body-bag, what the skeletal remains are, and then to determine what bones should be sent up for DNA analysis. In this case, samples were taken first, samples of the bones that you usually use for samples. And in the DNA samples, you might have noticed that there were some markings, 17A and 18A.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. And maybe this is a good time, Your Honours. I hate to interrupt the witness, but to take the break and we can finish with the DNA, and I think in 15 minutes I can finish her examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm asking that the witness be shown Exhibit 649. Okay. This is the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Doctor, I'd like you to look at -- I'm just going to show you -- I want you, please, to walk us as quickly through what -- just tell us about this document, what the number means in the corner, "KTA" number, and what the conclusion is of this report.

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: The first mark in the first square or box is the prosecution number attending my finding, 24806; the name of the location where the bodies were found; and the number of bodies "1/3". Then at the bottom we have the possible identity with a certain name, and underneath that, persons who gave blood. In this case, that was compared -- or rather the mother's and father's blood was compared to part of the bodily remains and bones that we found.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, you just said -- or it's recorded and I think you said: "... and the number of bodies '1/3'." Can you clarify for us what that means? Is that -- did you mean to say number of bodies or is that the number of the body, the "1/3"?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: I said, well, they're the bodily remains of one body, and that body was marked "1/3", and that was the marking on the bag in which that body was located.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So is it fair -- just so we're clear, this is body number 3 found at the location Kamenica, and does the "1" stand for "Kamenica"?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I've already emphasised that, that the "1", there's "1/1," "1/2," "1/3" because it's the same site, the same location where the bodies were found.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can we just move to the second page, please, and I'll just ask the witness a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And just briefly, and I think we can probably draw the conclusion ourself, but is this the DNA report for a body that was bagged in bag number 4; is that what this represents?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's it. Like the "1/3", this is "1/4".

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. May we go to the third page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And is this the DNA report for body number 8?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And may we move to the next report, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: This appears -- what is -- this is -- says "1/7". Again, can you tell us what this -- this is the second one?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: This is a body marked "1/7".

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, but we just saw 1/7. Is this a repeat, or is this another bone sample, or can you please explain why there are two reports for body --

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: "1/7", we did see, but in that second box down at the bottom, there was another sample. These are teeth, which means that this finding was sent in order to identify the skull.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, how many samples did you send to the ICMP laboratory of all of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Of all the bodies, we took 17 samples. But can I stress something here? These were preliminary samples, because I said that the bodies had not been completely examined. So this is the first step towards further identification and completing of the body, because in my -- can I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sure, of course.

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: In my findings, when describing the body 1/8, fragments of the skull were found, and they were marked as "1/8A" -- just a moment, please, just let me check -- and "1/8B" and "1/8C."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, did "A" correspond with the skull number or with the number of fragments from a different part of body 8?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: You mean where it says "Kamenica A, B and C"; is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No. What I'm asking for is what does the letter mean on these DNA reports when it comes after --

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: When from one body which we have in the bag -- when there's one body in the bag and you send two samples, to confirm whether the skull and the body belong to the same person, especially if there is doubt, then we have to separate this and say "1/7" separately of that body and then the next sample will be "1/7A," and send that in separate bags, separate small bags, for the laboratory to examine them and do the testing separately. Had we placed the bone and the tooth in bag 1/7, then the laboratory would just process one sample and then we won't have the right confirmation as to whether the skull and the body belongs to the same person.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. But when you have -- my understanding is that you had the skulls designated as "A" through "H," without the "G," so I don't want us to be confused. Skull A, is it different from bone sample 1/7A?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, because the markings are quite different. "1/8A" and here we only have "A."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. So if -- can we -- just to illustrate on -- can we move further in this document to where it says "Kamenica C"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we do --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you move, I just want to understand one thing, ma'am. What were the results of the testing on 1/7 and 1/7A?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not quite clear how you mean -- what you mean by this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What I want to find out is: Did the results show that sample 1/7 and 1/7A belonged to one and the same person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what they indicate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And 1/8, 1/8A, same thing, too, and 8B, if there is an 8B? I thought you referred to a "B" too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a "B" here, but 1/8 -- all I have is the finding for 1/8. 1/8A DNA, the result didn't come through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what about 1/8B; did the results come through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1/8B wasn't even sent out, because after the examination we found that there was a suspect bone which perhaps did not belong to that body, so that's why I said that this was preliminary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So 1/8B is not part of your testimony, because that was not sent out for testing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Had the body stayed with me, then after the processing I would have sent out samples as they were found on the body. However, as soon as the first findings arrived, that it was related to these persons, the bodies no longer stayed with me, so I wasn't able to complete the investigation or to follow it further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't understand your answer. I don't know whether you understood my question. I'm asking: Because you did not send sample 1/8B for testing, therefore that sample is excluded from your evidence? You're not going to tell us anything about it because --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't have the finding. All I can say is that 1/8B is a fragment of a bone subsequently found during the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Doctor, in preparation for your testimony, did you review all of the DNA reports that exist with relation to this, your examination?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: What I have here, the findings that I received, I looked through those; that is to say, I looked at the name, surname, the location, the identity as possible, to determine 99 per cent, the percentage I gave, and that's what we generally use and I use as a physician.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right, thank you. My question -- my specific question, though, is: You sent -- I believe you said earlier you sent out 17 samples, and you don't have 17 DNA reports, do you?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: No, I don't, and I don't think nobody has. I don't think they have arrived, because from the same burial site, you might have a year go by from one finding to another. That's how the ICPM works -- MP works. Sometimes if it's marked "Urgent" by the prosecutor, then you would receive findings more rapidly but not at the same time. Otherwise, it takes some time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many DNA reports that you have seen in relation to your examination, this particular examination, how many DNA final reports?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Nine. Let me check that again. Of those nine, three refer to one person, and two are also for one person, for Radomir Blagojevic. So in actual fact, five findings for two persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us the total number of persons that there have been findings for in these DNA reports?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Six, six persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. If I've understood you well, out of the 17 bones which you sent in so that a DNA analysis would be conducted, for nine of them you got an answer and for the remaining eight, you might still be getting an answer over the next few months or years perhaps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, maybe even longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, if we just do the math here, there are nine reports and six identifications, but three reports refer to one and two reports refer to another one. Can you tell us if, within those three reports or two reports for one person, whether any of the skulls that were found along with the skeletons, if they relate to any of the persons? And if so, which ones?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: For Blagojevic, Radomir Blagojevic, they coincide. The body number is "1/3" and the skull is "B."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And could we look at the report for Kamenica H? I'm not sure it's -- I think it's the last page of this series. It's ERN 25, so it would be the last page. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us about this finding, whether this -- this was a -- this was a skull; correct?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Yes, and it's an "H."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And in looking at the other DNA reports, there was no other -- there was no other body parts that -- at least that you examined and tested, that related to this skull; is that -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: In the finding, along with the skulls, there was part of the neck vertebrae. I'll have a look at that finding. I don't know it off by heart. Along with that skull, without the lower jaw, so the skull was missing a lower jaw, but, anyway, the first cervical vertebrae was found.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So can you tell us what number of body that is that goes with -- in other words, this is Kamenica H, which is -- you can tell us if this appears to be the -- the report says the skull of "Pejic Mladin." What body number is that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which part are you talking about now, Madam?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I thought she just identified the cervical part, another bone, and I don't see the report for Mr. Pejic. I'm asking her where that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, but where do you get Pejic from? You're talking about a report.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Right in front of you on the screen, Doctor, what is this DNA report for? Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Confirmation of identity on the basis of a tooth, which means from the skull, which confirms that that head belonged to Pejic, Mladin, or whatever the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. But I guess I just asked you if there were any other bones and what body number Mr. Pejic was assigned -- was assigned to this skull, but I -- and I don't see the report. If you could show us -- if you could tell us if you have a report on that.

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: From this report, you can't see that, because this report is just linked to this part, the tooth and the part of the skull.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. But if you could look through your other nine reports, Doctor, or the other eight reports, the DNA reports, and tell me if there is one that -- another one that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know what, Madam Sartorio --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- I think it would be simpler to say to this witness can she please match the letters with the numbers, and then we know who's who.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: If they match.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If they match.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: You've given us one match, Doctor, Blagojevic. Can you tell us if any of the other skulls match the body numbers, and which ones?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: We have another match with 1/7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're now into detailed discussion about the skulls, which is obviously an area which falls within the second part of the document, and it's been stated by the Trial Chamber that we're not to deal with those matters today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I'm sorry, my fault.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on, Your Honour, just quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, Doctor, I'd like to concentrate just briefly for a few questions on your report. May the witness please be shown the first part of her report, which is Exhibit 654.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm getting a little confused, ma'am. Has this witness's report been tendered into evidence already?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The first half, the bodies through 1/7, as 654, Exhibit 654.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Really?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: At the beginning, I asked her if she confirmed her report. No?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Page 55 through 70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page 55 through 70, was that the report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Just a minute, Your Honour. Apparently there's a technical problem, so -- but I -- I thought it had been -- is it admitted in evidence, it just doesn't have a number? We need to bring up P02964, page 55 through 70, again. But I thought it had been assigned -- I wrote "654" on it, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mrs. Sartorio, can you confirm that the expert's report is indeed P2964?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It's contained within the range of 2964. There's a -- the ERN range of that document runs 34 pages, and the first half of the doctor's report is in that range, and it's pages 55 through 70 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would like to see page 55.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. It's page 27 -- or 26 in the Bosnian language, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, is this it on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which was Exhibit 653.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I've been told to -- it's going to be worked out, the numbers. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fifty-five to 70 was Exhibit 654.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay, I would like the witness to look at it. The Bosnian version is up on the screen, but the English is not yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. I would like the witness to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is this the first page of --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, there's actually a cover page with the doctor's name on it, but this is the first page of the substantive report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I've been reading the cover page. That's why [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. I want the witness, please, to see the last sentence of her report with regard to body 1/1, so it's the second page in English, and scroll down in Bosnian, please. I think we need to go -- the next page in English, please. It's the end of the -- before you see "1/2." Okay, so it would be the next page in Bosnian as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay, Doctor, I'd like to direct your attention to -- to your last sentence with regard to body 1/1 and ask you if you would read it and if you have any comments on what you wrote.

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: "Death was probably violent and arrived as a result of the complete interruption of the continuity of the cervical spine, which also resulted in separation of the head from the body."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you arrived at this conclusion?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: By examining the body remains, body parts, where I deal with injuries and changes, and it says that the body of the sixth cervical vertebrae, in the lower half, was cut off with a smooth blade incorporating the right side of the body and that certain parts are lacking. The lower edge and lower adjacent edge has impairments to the plate. The findings whereby this was a smooth blade cutting off the cervical vertebrae in a sweep cuts the continuity between the body and the head.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, just a question. We spoke earlier, I believe, and also at a prior occasion on -- based on your limited examination, given the nature of what your task was, were you able to determine what actually caused the death of this person? And if -- and what do you mean by this last sentence?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Cause of death -- the exact cause of death cannot be established exactly, because a lot of time went by for us to be able to say whether the cross-sections cut off that were found, whether they were caused during life or immediately after death. This last portion explains the fact that that could be a possible cause of death, because injuries of this type found on a body and left that way would bring about death ultimately.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: In other words, you can't have life with a complete interruption of continuity of the cervical spine, can you?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: In order for you to reach this vertebra, because the vertebrae are in the posterior part of the neck, you have to cut through the soft tissue, through the blood vessels, and you have to penetrate the respiratory tract, and this is more than enough to cause death.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But if this could have been done -- could this have been done after death, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: It could have.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Based on your examination, you are unable to determine if it was before or after death, are you?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: It was too long ago in order for anybody to be able to say with any degree of certainty whether this was done during life or after death. There was no vital tissue, there was no vital reaction in order to tell us that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Just a few more questions. May the witness be shown the end of number 2, 1/2, please, which is page 4 -- top of the page 4 in English. It's the end of section 1/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, Doctor, I'd like you to read the next-to-the-last sentence, to the sentence that talks about taking the DNA, and ask you if you can comment on what your conclusion was in this report with regard to this body.

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: A fracture of the lower joint part of the left calf bone, which is the beneath-the-knee bone, with the damage inflicted to the bone surface after the death and the damage of the interior upper part of the left shin bone. When I talk about damage, in our findings we mostly refer to the damage inflicted after death, either when the body was moved or as a result of humidity in the grave, and mostly as a result of that, these surfaces are damaged, they are not fractured to indicate a trauma. They are damaged rather than fractured.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. So this is -- When you refer to this, you mean this damage was inflicted by something -- well, strike that. You already answered that other question, I believe. May the witness now be shown the last part of the examination report on 1/4, please. Thank you. Now, if you could read, Doctor, the next-to-the-last sentence of your findings under "1/4". And again you refer to -- you say death was probably violent, and -- at least that's what the English says. I'd like you to confirm what it says in the Bosnian language and what you mean by this.

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: "The above-described cuts of the part of vertebra and both shin-bones indicate an action delivered by a swinging blade of a hard mechanical object. The death was probably violent and caused by the interrupted functioning of the cervical spine and the severance of the head." Again, in this body, when it comes to the changes and injuries, we found a linear cut on the lateral side of the third cervical vertebra with a cut of the bone of the lower anterior part of the body. Again, we found changes on the cervical vertebra, and as I've already told you, in order to reach the vertebra, you have to damage the very important vital parts of the body that can be found in the neck.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And just two other sections I'd like you to you comment on, Doctor. The end of the report on 1/6, if you would.

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: The death was probably violent and caused by a politrauma. In this body, we found several fractures, as can be seen from the findings; a fracture of the ribs, of the shoulder bone, of the femur, and the lower leg bones, which means that there were multiple fractures which translates as politrauma in our diagnosis, or several mechanical injuries.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions of this witness, Your Honour, on this part of her report. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Sartorio. Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Doctor. My name is Nicholas Robson, and I'll be asking you some questions on behalf of General Delic. So, Doctor, could you just confirm that your involvement in this matter began when you performed the autopsy at the morgue at Visoko?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: My involvement in this started when we first took samples for the DNA analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And that was during the autopsy which you performed together with Dr. Karan; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: It is not correct. We did not do the autopsy together. We only took the samples together. Once the samples were taken, I did the exam together with my assistant.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Do you know, were photographs taken of the exhumation site prior to the autopsy taking place?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: Based on my long experience with exhumations, every exhumation is photographed; the grave, before it is dug out, when the grave is open and the bodies are exposed. When the body is cleaned, another photo is taken. Then when the body is placed in a bag, before the transportation another photo is taken with the markings on the bag. So this is the series of photos that are taken on the ground and that concern the exhumation process.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: As I understand your answer, you say in general, photographs are taken of the exhumation site, but do you know, in this specific case, were photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson, the reason is because she says she didn't attend the exhumation, so she wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it may be the photographs were presented as -- to the witness at some stage, and that's what I'm trying to establish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then the question should be: Did you see any photographs of the exhumation, if any at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Can you answer what Judge Moloto just stated? Did you see any photographs of this exhumation site?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Now, according to your witness statement, you said that DNA samples were taken from the femur of the bodies, and in relation to the skulls, DNA samples were taken from the teeth; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: I don't understand one part of your question. What has the femur got to do with the skull? You said something of the femur that had to do something with the skull. What did you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I think that was the translation of my question. I'll break it down. In relation to the bodies, is it right that the DNA sample was taken from the femur, in general?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
utterances.text: That's common practice. If teeth are missing, then the laboratory recommends that the DNA sample be taken from the femur bone, because the femur is the easiest for the extraction of the DNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: And in relation to the skulls, the DNA sample was taken from one of the -- one of the teeth?

utterances.speaker: SABIHA SILAJDZIC-BRKIC
